canonical_claim: CAS's single true read-side correctness hole (labeled X1/R1, "missing read"): a ref-less/cross-node reader resolves ref to manifest to blob-location at plan time, discards the manifest, then performs a deferred, unpinned blob GET later; if the ref is dropped and GC completes condemn to pending to delete before that GET fires, a committed datum becomes unreadable mid-query (`NoSuchKey`). This is bounded to the write/GC plane being otherwise loss-free; the fix direction is an ephemeral reader pin folded into the GC mark/ack-floor union, or bounding query lifetime below the condemn-to-delete latency.

evidence.notes: NoSuchKey occurs in backend exception handling and in a test for a mid-GET missing object.

canonical_claim: CAS's security perimeter is exactly the S3 bucket credential: there is no intra-pool authorization, identities are self-asserted and unsigned, and blobs are shared pool-wide by content hash with no namespace in the blob key. Combined with non-cryptographic CityHash128 content-addressing and reads that never re-verify payload-against-key, this enables SEC-1 (High) collision poisoning: because dedup is HEAD-first and blobs are pool-global, an attacker who can craft a `CityHash128` collision can pre-seed a poisoned blob under the victim's future hash so a victim in a different table/tenant later writing the benign content dedups to the poison and reads attacker bytes, with all CRC checks passing (latent in a single-trust-domain pool, real the moment a pool is multi-tenant).

evidence.notes: CityHash128 occurs as the tested default blob-hash path.
